official.deadline_note: Published wording: 'International Master's Programmes: The application period for studies starting in autumn 2027 is from 5 to 19 January 2027.' The application form closes at 15:00 (UTC+2) on the closing day. The university has not yet published the attachment deadline for the 2027 round; in the autumn 2026 round the application closed 16 Jan 2026 and attachments were due 23 Jan 2026 at 15:00 (UTC+2).
official.status_note: The published application period for International Master's Programmes starting in autumn 2027 runs from 5 to 19 January 2027, so the round is announced but not yet open at the time of verification.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'The fees for the University of Helsinki Master's Programmes in English are 13,000, 15,000 and 18,000 EUR per academic year, depending on the programme.' The scholarship section states: 'Tuition fees range from 13 000 to 18 000 euros.' The waiver reduces the fee to zero (100%) or half (50%); it does not pay cash.
benefits: Tuition fee waiver covering 50 % or 100 % of the tuition fee; the majority of scholarships available are 50 % tuition fee waivers
Duration of the scholarship is two years
Waiver covers also the second study year of the Master's degree in case the student has completed at least 55 credits during the first academic year
Graduates of English-language bachelor's programmes continuing to a Helsinki master's receive a waiver automatically by GPA: minimum 3.8/5 for 100 %, 3.4-3.7/5 for 50 %
Dean's award of 1.000 EUR may be awarded to second and third year students in English-language bachelor's programmes (no waivers for bachelor's applicants)
eligibility: You are eligible for the Master's programme at the University of Helsinki
You are liable for tuition fees: citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who do not have permanent residence status in Finland are liable for tuition fees
You meet the requirements for obtaining an entry visa and residence permit for Finland
You have obtained excellent results in your previous studies and can prove this in your application
Students not liable to pay tuition fees (EU/EEA/Swiss citizens or exempt permit holders) cannot apply for a waiver
requirements: Eligible for the Master's programme at the University of Helsinki (a completed first-cycle bachelor's degree or equivalent; conditional admission possible if graduation is still pending)
Liable to pay tuition fees, i.e. a citizen of a non-EU/EEA country without permanent residence status in Finland
Meet the requirements for obtaining an entry visa and residence permit for Finland
Excellent results in previous studies that can be proved in the application
Study full time and earn at least 55 ECTS per academic year to fulfil the scholarship requirements
Accept the scholarship agreement before the scholarship comes into effect
documents: Online application form submitted on Studyinfo (one form, maximum three master's programmes)
Bachelor's degree certificate and transcript of records for the bachelor's degree, plus educational documents for other relevant higher education studies
Official translations of educational documents not issued in English, Finnish or Swedish, submitted together with the originals
Copy of passport, residence permit card or photo ID
Proof of English language proficiency using one of the university's accepted methods
Programme-specific attachments listed in the programme's admission criteria on Studyinfo
selection_criteria: Tuition fee waivers for new students are awarded on the basis of academic overall assessment
Previous academic performance and possible letters of motivation
The grounds presented by applicants in their grant applications
Academic excellence and success in previous studies according to the general master's degree entrance requirements
Motivation to study in a master's programme at the University of Helsinki
University's and programmes' strategic goals can also be taken into account
coverage: 50 % or 100 % of the tuition fee for two years
No coverage of living expenses - the university states it does not offer scholarships to cover living expenses
application_method: Find the Master's programme you want to apply to
See the instructions on how to apply to the Master's programme and prepare the necessary attachments
Apply for a tuition fee waiver with the same application form used to apply to the Master's programme (there are no separate scholarship application forms)
official.application_route: Apply to an International Master's Programme on Studyinfo.fi during the single annual application period and request the tuition fee waiver inside the same application form.
official.study_mode: Full-time; students are required to study full time and earn at least 55 ECTS per academic year
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who do not have permanent residence status in Finland; must meet the requirements for obtaining an entry visa and residence permit for Finland
official.international_eligibility: Open to international (non-EU/EEA) applicants only; scholarships are intended for excellent tuition fee-liable students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens are not liable to pay tuition fees and cannot apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction beyond applying to an International Master's Programme at the University of Helsinki. Applicants to English-language bachelor's programmes receive no tuition fee waiver.
official.duration: Two years (120 ECTS, two years of full-time study)
official.description: The University of Helsinki scholarship programme consists of tuition fee waivers, waiving the tuition fee for 50 % or 100 %. Scholarships are intended for excellent tuition fee-liable students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who want to complete a Master's programme at the University of Helsinki.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver, 50 % or 100 %, decided together with the admission result
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with a minimum of 6.0 in writing (only IELTS Academic accepted, not General); TOEFL iBT 92 with a minimum of 22 in writing; PTE Academic 62 overall with a minimum of 54 in each communicative skills section; Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency at pass level; National Certificate of Language Proficiency (YKI) level 5 in all sub-tests; or an accepted upper-secondary or university degree completed in English. Statements issued by individual language teachers or universities' own language test scores are not accepted, and requirements from different tests cannot be combined.

not_confirmed: The exact tuition fee charged by each individual programme (the page gives 13,000, 15,000 and 18,000 EUR per academic year 'depending on the programme' and points to Studyinfo for the programme-specific fee)
The monetary value of an individual award, because the waiver is a percentage of a programme-specific fee (a 50 % waiver equals roughly half of that programme's annual fee)
The number of waivers, or the number of 100 % waivers, available in any given round
The 2027-round deadline for uploading application attachments (only the autumn 2026 round dates are published at present)
The scholarship categories are still labelled 'for application round 2025-26' on the official page, so the 50 %/100 % category labels themselves are stated for the previous round
verification.notes: Checked the University of Helsinki scholarship programme page, the Apply to International Master's Programmes hub, the How to apply schedule, the Required application attachments instructions and the Proving your English language skills page, all on helsinki.fi. The 2027 application window (5-19 January 2027) and the 13,000/15,000/18,000 EUR fee figures are stated directly on the official domain; fee figures and deadlines were cross-checked across two official pages.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a cash scholarship: it is a reduction of the University of Helsinki tuition bill to 50 % or 100 % for the two years of your master's, decided by the same academic panel that assesses your admission. You apply for it by ticking the waiver request inside the normal Studyinfo application between 5 and 19 January 2027 - there is no separate form and no separate deadline. Plan on funding your entire life in Helsinki from your own resources, because the university explicitly offers nothing towards living costs and only a small minority of waivers are for the full 100 %.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with a strong bachelor's transcript and a clear study motivation who can personally cover roughly EUR 9,000-13,000 a year of living costs on top of any waived tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are actually tuition-fee liable: check your residence permit history against the Migri-based exemptions on the official page before investing time in the application, because a type A permit granted earlier for studying does not exempt you

Register the programme-specific attachment list from the programme's admission criteria on Studyinfo.fi and build those documents first - some programmes require a portfolio or reference and a missing mandatory attachment is an automatic rejection

Sit the English test well before early January and make sure the score stays valid past the supplement deadline, since test results take weeks to publish and cannot be stitched together from two different tests

Request your bachelor's transcript and degree certificate early, and check they list course names, grades and the name of the degree being awarded - a transcript without course names is rejected outright
Budget the one-off 100 EUR national application fee, the HYY student union membership fee and the Kela/FSHS student healthcare fee alongside your living-cost estimate
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a waiver is a living allowance and arriving in Finland without proof of roughly EUR 9,000-13,000 per year for rent, food, transport and insurance - Migri requires that money regardless of the waiver

Uploading extra goodwill documents such as unsolicited recommendation letters or certificates; the university states additional attachments are not evaluated and slow processing, which can cost you time you do not have
Sending documents by email or by post during the application stage instead of attaching them to the Studyinfo form - email and courier only apply to conditionally admitted applicants
Applying for a 100 % waiver in a programme whose scholarship policy only ever awards 50 % waivers, then losing the whole offer because the unfunded half of the fee could not be paid by the deadline
Losing the waiver after enrolment by dropping below 55 ECTS in the first year, or by acquiring an EU/EEA-linked residence status that removes tuition-fee liability
Letting the fee-liability change silently: the university rechecks residence permit history from Migri during the application period, so an undisclosed earlier study permit can flip your status late
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition. You must self-fund living costs (rent, meals, transport, insurance and personal expenses), the one-off 100 EUR application fee, the HYY student union membership fee and the Kela/FSHS student healthcare fee, plus any programme-specific study materials. A 50 % waiver still leaves half of a 13,000-18,000 EUR annual fee payable.
document_audit: Transcripts must name courses, show grades and state the degree programme being completed - course codes alone are not accepted and require a syllabus supplement

Translations must be official translator or issuing-institution translations, stamped and signed on every page, and must be uploaded alongside the original-language document; a translation without the original is void

Official translations and certified copies become mandatory only after a conditional admission (29 May for complete degrees, 31 August for incomplete ones) - but a plain scan at application stage is what makes the offer conditional in the first place
Your passport name must match your educational documents and language test; a mismatch requires an official name-change document such as a marriage certificate
Applicants who also studied in Finland must upload those records too, or the studies are ignored in the evaluation
alerts: The waiver is decided with the admission result and communicated in the official acceptance email - it is not a separate later decision you can chase
You must sign the scholarship agreement to activate it, and a 100 % waiver holder still has to complete enrolment while a 50 % holder must also pay the remaining half
The tuition fee for the first academic year has historically fallen due on 31 August - well after admission - so a 50 % waiver holder must have the balance ready by late summer
Liability to pay tuition fees is judged on your residence permit history and is always verified with Finnish Migration Services, so past study permits in Finland count against you

Applications to English-language bachelor's programmes receive no waiver at all, and only the GPA route (3.8/5 for 100 %, 3.4-3.7/5 for 50 %) exists for bachelor's graduates moving up to a Helsinki master's
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One application form on Studyinfo.fi covering up to three master's programmes, submitted between 5 and 19 January 2027 with the waiver request included, attachments uploaded to the same form soon after, then academic assessment in March and results from early April.
